ostrzezenia.tekst: According to ANSES, the French food safety agency, the foods that most often cause botulism include canned vegetables, such as peppers, asparagus, Greek-style olives and tapenade, and canned meat, such as terrine and pâté, usually homemade or artisanal. [T:OLE-046]
According to ANSES, the French food safety agency, keeping the cold chain is essential for foods that are cooked but not sterilized, such as pâté and ready meals. [T:OLE-047]
Boiling is not enough to sterilize food, because Clostridium botulinum spores resist even boiling water. [T:OLE-048]
